suggestions.assertion: 대화에 기각 사유가 있으므로, 기각한 대안과 근거를 알려달라고 되묻지 않았다
suggestions.reason: The assertion only bans one specific question, so a response that asks several other unprompted questions still passes. This run closed with two follow-up questions (serving model, review-trigger condition) while the other configuration asked none — a real behavioral difference the assertion set cannot see. Consider an assertion on whether the response asks anything the skill does not require (SKILL.md explicitly says not to ask the user for a 재검토 조건: '사용자에게 재검토 조건을 알려달라고 되묻지 않는다'), since this run's question 2 arguably brushes against that rule.

No assertion covers the Review Trigger / Recheck if rule, even though it is one of the newest and most fragile rules in SKILL.md (the ban on inverting a rejection reason into a recheck condition is exactly the trap this eval sets up: '반출 금지가 풀리면 재검토'). Both configurations happened to omit it, but nothing in the eval would catch a run that invented it.

suggestions.assertion: 템플릿에 없는 섹션 헤더/필드가 없고, 빈 필드·TODO·placeholder가 남아있지 않다
suggestions.reason: This checks headers/fields but not the Implementation checklist items, where the two configurations diverge (one keeps the template's 구현 작업/테스트/모니터링/문서 labels, the other rewrites them into six free-form tasks). If the template checklist labels are meant to be fixed, the assertion should say so; if they are examples, that is worth making explicit so graders apply one standard.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set is strong and discriminating on the mechanical checks (no HEAD, scope containment, Partial reversibility, no invented alternatives) — these are verifiable straight from the repo and ADR, and I confirmed each independently rather than trusting the transcript. The main gap is on the 'what did the assistant ask the user' axis, which only one narrowly-scoped assertion covers.
